labels.label: bzprop:c3s1p1_facette_ouverte
labels.notes: Paper (benzecri1960_ch3.tex:141-144): a facette F of a convex W is open in its support L with L's finest locally convex topology. Lean facette_isOpen: for an arbitrary real vector space E (no topology, any dimension), Convex W, IsFacette W F (= F is the F_W-class of a point of W, Def. 2 of the strict Facettes module), and EVERY P : E, the set {v in direction(affineSpan F) | v + P in F} is open for finestLC of the direction. Taking P in L this is exactly F open in L under the chart v |-> v + P, for every origin, so the reading does not depend on the origin; for P outside L the set is empty. No added hypothesis, no narrowed conclusion. Second reading facette_isOpen_induced (L as a subtype of E with the topology induced by finestLC E) is also proved, and induced_finestLC_eq_finestLC proves the two topologies agree, so the reading is settled in both directions and the mark is legitimate. finestLC is genuine: defined as the seminorm topology of ALL seminorms, it is a member of LCTopologies (IsTopologicalAddGroup + ContinuousSMul R + LocallyConvexSpace R, the standard notion of a locally convex TVS) and below every member (isLeast_finestLC; finestLC_le), so the class is nonempty and the least element is in it, not vacuous; also T2. isOpen_finestLC_iff_core (convex C open iff every point is a core point) and isOpen_finestLC_iff_finiteDimensional (convex C open iff for each x in C and each finite-dimensional subspace l, {u in l | x+u in C} is a moduleTopology-neighbourhood of 0, i.e. x interior to (x+l) cap C in x+l) are correct statements and carry the convexity they need. Instance real: isFacette_openSquare (]0,1[^2 is a facette of [0,1]^2), openSquare_isOpen is facette_isOpen applied to it, finestLC_prod : finestLC (R x R) = instTopologicalSpaceProd (via finestLC_eq_of_finiteDimensional), openSquare_isOpen_finestLC. The proof-gap finding is accurate: the printed reduction to finite-dimensional l (l.146-149) is valid for convex sets (proved here with Convex as hypothesis), and nothing before Prop. 1 in Ch. 3 § 1 (Defs. 1-2, the Remark) states that a facette is convex; the Lean proof sidesteps it by applying the convex criterion to {v | v + P in W} and then add_mem_facette_of_two. It is correctly reported as a missing step in the proof, not an error in the statement. Docstring contract (lean-causal/kb/entries/0006, per CAMPAIGN.md): title, mark with `benzecri1960_ch3.tex:141` within the first 4000 characters, French quote, Hypothesis checklist (all carried, true), SCOPE (readings, helpers, S(E) transfer l.276-280 excluded and outside this label), provenance line. FinestLocallyConvex.lean names the label only unmarked and says it certifies none by itself: correct.
